findings.title: Rationale for unparseable review files does not carry forward the arch's "names the parse failure explicitly" requirement
findings.description: The architecture states, under "File-read failure modes": *"A review file that exists but cannot be parsed… must not silently pass. It is treated as UNKNOWN and `review_unknown_as` applies. The rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly."* The slice design handles the *status* side of this correctly (TD-2, Special Considerations: present-but-unparseable ⇒ UNKNOWN ⇒ `review_unknown_as`, surfaced as `review-failed`, never `pending`). However, TD-7 — which is the slice's normative spec for what the rationale must contain — enumerates only "the review type; for `review-failed`, also the verdict and threshold that produced the block." For an unparseable file the normalized verdict is `UNKNOWN`, so under this spec the rationale would say "verdict UNKNOWN does not clear threshold …" rather than naming the parse/read failure. The arch's requirement that the rationale *name the parse failure explicitly* is therefore left unmet by the slice's rationale contract. Success Criteria likewise only asserts the file is "treated as UNKNOWN (never silently cleared)" and does not require parse-failure-naming in the rationale. TD-7 should be extended to require, for the present-but-unreadable case, a rationale that names the parse/read failure (e.g. "review artifact could not be parsed"), distinct from a clean `UNKNOWN`-verdict rationale.

findings.title: Inert `review_type` per-gate keys in tension with arch's fail-fast principle, sanctioned by slice plan
findings.description: The architecture lists "Fail-fast on configuration errors" as a principle: *"an unrecognized per-gate config is a config error surfaced immediately, not a silent pass or silent block."* TD-4 leaves the 240-shipped `workflow.review_gates.{gate}.review_type` keys *defined but unread*, delegating deprecation docs to 243 — so a user who sets a malformed `review_type` value gets no immediate error. This is a mild tension with the arch's fail-fast principle, but it is explicitly sanctioned by the slice plan ("241 leaves them defined-but-unread… OR 241 removes them; the design makes that call"), and the backward-compatibility rationale is sound. No action required; flagged only so the trade-off is visible. If the team prefers the clean removal path TD-4 also offers, that would also satisfy fail-fast.

findings.title: Position-derived review-type model and 244 fold-in align with slice plan and arch boundaries
findings.description: The slice implements exactly the model the slice plan's Notes mandate: review type derived from lifecycle position (arch/slice/tasks/code at the four boundaries), never configured, with the retired slice 244 folded in as the `arch`/pre-slice-plan case. The `BOUNDARY_REVIEW_TYPE` const is the single source of truth, satisfying the project's "define once" convention. This supersedes the arch's per-gate `reviewType` config as the slice plan explicitly authorizes. Boundary→signal mapping (file presence for three boundaries, `STATUS.Complete` checkbox completion for the code boundary) keeps CF artifact-shaped and respects the arch's layer boundary (CF does not inspect git/commits/PRs), matching TD-5 and the slice plan's note on the code trigger.

findings.title: Dependency direction and integration points match consuming/providing slice expectations
findings.description: `reviewGate.ts` is standalone (pure functions + one config reader), imported by the navigator and reused by 242 without importing the navigator — correct DRY direction. `ConfigManager` is constructor-injected as an optional dependency, preserving all existing call paths and keeping worktree scope inherited from the surfaces' already-resolved paths (consistent with 180's resolution chain the arch references). Provides (`reviewGate` evaluator, `pending-review`/`review-failed` statuses, `review`/`blocked` vocabulary, `STATUS` const, injected-navigator pattern) and consumes (240's detection slot, config keys, reserved branch, `parseFrontmatter`) match what 242/243/910 and 240 expect. The `NextAction` return type is preserved (additive recommendation strings only), satisfying the arch's stability constraint for Amoeba. The `parseFrontmatter` never-throws contract relied on by TD-2 is verified against the actual parser.

findings.title: Scope is proportional; deferred scope is correctly bounded
findings.description: The slice is the behavioral core (effort 4/5 per plan) and its mechanism count is justified: one evaluator module, two new statuses, one const introduction, four surface wirings, boundary wiring. Exclusions are explicit and match the slice plan — ConsistencyChecker wiring → 242, docs → 243, the ~50-site `NormalizedStatus` literal sweep → 910, score enforcement → 301. No scope assigned to this slice is dropped (all four boundaries are covered, including the folded-in 244), and no out-of-scope mechanism (e.g. the consistency rule, score enforcement) is pulled in. The `STATUS` const is introduced and used only in new code, with the mechanical sweep deliberately deferred so a large no-behavior diff doesn't bury the gate-logic review — the same proportionality rationale 240 used.
